---

This site is a [Quarto](https://quarto.org) website, edited in RStudio and hosted
on GitHub Pages. The whole thing is plain text — `.qmd` files plus one YAML config
— which means it versions cleanly in git and anything I can compute in R can go
straight into a page.

## Adding a post

Each post is a folder under `posts/` containing an `index.qmd`:

```
posts/
  welcome/index.qmd
  my-new-post/
    index.qmd
    a-figure.png
```

The folder-per-post layout keeps images next to the text that uses them, and the
published URL comes out as `/posts/my-new-post/`.

The front matter needs four things:

``` yaml
---
title: "The title"
description: "One line that shows up on the blog listing."
date: 2026-09-01
categories: [rstats, notes]
---
```

Then **Render** in RStudio, and the post appears on the [blog page](../../blog.qmd)
automatically — the listing reads the `posts/` folder, so there's no index to
update by hand.

## Why Quarto over R Markdown

Mostly that the website machinery is built in rather than bolted on, that
`freeze: auto` means old posts don't re-run their code on every build, and that
the same `.qmd` can render to HTML, PDF, or slides without changing the source.
